title: Russian forces occupy Gori after the Sarkozy ceasefire
body:
Gori, a Georgian military and transport hub on the main east-west highway, was hit by Russian air raids from 8 August 2008. Georgian forces entered the town on 10 August and withdrew on 11 August. On 13 August, several hours after the ceasefire negotiated by French President Nicolas Sarkozy, Russian forces captured Gori, and Russian armour then moved toward Tbilisi and stopped about an hour's drive away.

Georgia said about 60 civilians were killed in a 9 August raid, while Russia said it had hit an armament depot. On 12 August a raid killed seven people and wounded over 30 according to media.ge, and Dutch journalist Stan Storimans was among the dead; Human Rights Watch attributed his death to cluster munitions. Russia's deputy chief of the General Staff, Anatoliy Nogovitsyn, did not admit the raid.

On 14 August Russia said it would hand control back to Georgian police, but the patrols broke down the same day. Human Rights Watch documented pillaging, assaults and abductions by South Ossetian forces. Georgia and Western governments said the occupation violated the ceasefire, while Russian UN ambassador Vitaly Churkin said Russian forces "are not in Gori". Russian troops began leaving Gori on 22 August, and Georgian police re-entered the city. At least 56,000 Georgian refugees were reported by CNN.
